title: the top level of a ply.yaml document
description: The normative definition of ply.yaml (The-Ply-Spec.md §5; §5 is this file's prose rendering, and any divergence is a bug in §5). Ply embeds this file in the binary and never reads a schema from the target workspace: editing an on-disk copy changes nothing at runtime. The shipped copy exists as read-only reference and for IDE tooling. Two constraints are stated here declaratively and enforced at runtime by hand-written code -- the check-string pattern (by ply_core::model::parse_check) and the code-path pattern (by ply_core::check::is_valid_path_form) -- and each is held to this file by an invariant test that walks a corpus and fails on the first disagreement (crates/ply-core/tests/schema.rs).

ply.description: Schema version. The grammar evolves only through Ply releases and this field; a value this build does not speak is E0201.

components.description: The component tree. A component name is unique across ALL merged files (E0202); nested names are qualified by their parent, so only siblings can collide.

externals.description: Named outside parties -- systems or people this codebase talks to but Ply can never verify. Top-level only: an external has no interior and cannot nest. Shares the component reference namespace (§5.1a rule 6).

edges.description: Edge strings (§5 item 2): "a -> b" declares that component a may call component b; "a ~> b : path::Type" declares a data flow. Deliberately carries no pattern: the language is not regular enough to state twice without one copy lying, so the parser (ply_core::model::parse_edge) is the single definition and a malformed edge is E0203, which names the expected form.

deny.description: Deny strings (§5 item 3): "PAT -> PAT [except C1, C2]" where PAT is an identifier or *. Carries no pattern, for the same reason as `edges`; a malformed rule is E0203.

profiles.description: Named sets of bans a component may opt into via `profile:`.

unresolved.description: Registry entries for open decisions with no code anchor. Ids are unique across the whole merged workspace, registry and fn entries together (E0205).

identifier.description: §5.1a rule 2: component, external and profile names are snake_case ASCII.

code_path.description: §5.1a rule 3: a plain segment path, where a segment may also be a type name in Type::method position. No generics, no trait-qualified paths, no lifetimes -- anything else is E0304, naming the construct.

check_string.description: §5 item 1 and §5.1a rule 4: test | fuzz(N) | bounded(K) | prove | mutate, with 1 <= N <= 1000000 and 1 <= K <= 64. Out of range, or any other form, is E0203.

capability.description: §5.1: the capabilities a component may declare it uses.

ban.description: §5.1: the bans a profile may impose.

anchor.description: The crate or crate::module::path this component is. Every component anchors to real code; an unresolvable anchor is E0301.

strict.description: Item-level architecture violations become errors rather than warnings (D4).

uses.description: The capabilities this component is allowed to use.

owns.description: Types only this component may mutate.

profile.description: Names a declared profile whose bans apply to this component.

checks.description: Default checks for every fn in scope that declares none of its own. A fn's own non-empty list replaces this entirely -- there is no merge.

fns.description: Fn claims, keyed by path relative to the anchor. Impl methods use Type::method.

external.title: an external
external.description: A name plus a sentence -- there is nothing else to declare, because an external carries no verdict, no ceiling, no checks, and is not a node of the §7 verdict tree.

note.description: What this outside party is, in a sentence. Required: a bare name tells a newbie nothing.

checks.description: The checks that govern this fn. `mutate` needs a `test` or `fuzz` entry in this same list, else E0504.

mode.description: check (default) verifies the body you wrote; synth (M6) writes the body from the contract.

requires.description: Precondition expressions, ANDed with any inline #[ply::requires] attributes.

ensures.description: Postcondition expressions, ANDed with any inline #[ply::ensures] attributes.

examples.description: Rust `==` expressions, compiled as plain #[test]s and never translated for an engine.

check_with.description: Concrete types for generic parameters (§5.4b), keyed by parameter name.

trusted.description: Externally-attested claims (§5.4d): believed on the strength of named evidence, never machine-checked by Ply.

unresolved.description: Open decisions attached to this fn.

entry.description: Names of the externals that can reach this fn. Each must resolve to a declared external, else E0209.

evidence.description: What attests it -- a named artifact a reviewer can go and read.

id.description: §5.1a rule 5: a positive integer, unique across the whole merged workspace. A duplicate is E0205.

note.description: The open decision, in a sentence.
